newsitem.title: USA: Calif. business owners see economic growth - survey.
newsitem.headline: Calif. business owners see economic growth - survey.

text.p: Most small-business owners in California foresee stable or expanding economic growth in the state through 1998, according to a Home Savings of America survey released on Thursday.

More than two-thirds, or 69 percent, of respondents who own a business with annual revenues of $1 million or less said they expected the California economy to remain on its current growth trend or accelerate through 1998, the survey found.
In addition, 52 percent of respondents said they felt the prospects for their own businesses would improve over the next two years, while 30 percent predicted stable growth.
Just 11 percent of business owners said they worry that prospects will not improve over the next two years, according to the survey.

"This survey of small businesses indicates the clear resurgence in California's economy," said Carl Forsythe, executive vice president and director of personal financial services for Home Savings of America. "Optimism among this important sector is strong and signals the undeniable recovery of California's vital job-creating businesses."

The survey was conducted by Fairbank, Maslin, Maullin and Associates between October 4 and 11 and included interviews with 793 randomly sampled small-business owners in Los Angeles, Sacramento, San Diego, San Francisco and in the central valley. Sampling error was plus or minus four percent.
Home Savings of America, a unit of H.F. Ahmanson and Co, is California's third largest financial services institution.
